utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-75-I, the Prosecutor versus Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hadzic, could I first check that you are following the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If at any moment you are not receiving interpretation, please let us know immediately. For record we need your vocal response, Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then could I have the appearances. For the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BRAMMERTZ
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Serge Brammertz for the Prosecution, together with Ken Scott and Aixa Jahnsen Lecca.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. Vladimir Petrovic, attorney-at-law, as duty counsel for Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Petrovic, to you. Mr. Hadzic, would you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Goran Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is the date and place of your birth, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 7 September 1958.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And your birthplace?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vinkovci.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm Judge O-Gon Kwon from South Korea. Mr. Hadzic, I understand that your family and the embassy of the country of which you are a national, i.e., Serbia, have been informed about your transfer to, and detention in, the United Nations Detention Unit of the Tribunal in Scheveningen, The Hague. Could you confirm that my understanding is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your understanding is correct. I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hadzic. This is the initial appearance of Mr. Goran Hadzic upon his transfer to the Tribunal. The hearing is to be conducted in accordance with Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal. The original indictment against the accused was confirmed on 4th of July, 2004, and made public on 16th July 2004. The indictment has since been amended and the now-operative indictment was filed on 22nd July 2011. On 21st of July, 2011, I, as the Acting President, assigned this case to Trial Chamber II, composed of Judges Delvoie, Hall, and Mindua. It is my understanding that that Chamber has decided that Judge Guy Delvoie from the Kingdom of Belgium will preside over the case; however, because of the judicial recess, I have assigned myself for the purpose of this initial appearance. Before we move further, I would like to inform you, Mr. Hadzic, that you have a fundamental right to remain silent throughout these proceedings and it will not be held against you. Is this understood?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Further, Articles 20 and 21 of the Statute of the International Tribunal guarantee the accused a number of rights, which I will now ask the Registrar to read out in full.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Article 20: Commencement and conduct of trial proceedings. "1. The Trial Chambers shall ensure that a trial is fair and expeditious and that proceedings are conducted in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, with full respect for the rights of the accused and due regard for the protection of victims and witnesses. "2. A person against whom an indictment has been confirmed shall, pursuant to an order or an arrest warrant of the International Tribunal, be taken into custody, immediately informed of the charges against him, and transferred to the International Tribunal. "3. The Trial Chamber shall read the indictment, satisfy itself that the rights of the accused are respected, confirm that the accused understands the indictment, and instruct the accused to enter a plea. The Trial Chamber shall then set the date for trial. "4. The hearings shall be public unless the Trial Chamber decides to close the proceedings in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Evidence." Article 21: Rights of the accused. "1. All persons shall be equal before the International Tribunal. "2. In the determination of charges against him, the accused shall be entitled to a fair and public hearing, subject to Article 22 of the Statute. "3. The accused shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to the provisions of the present Statute. "4. In the determination of any charge against the accused pursuant to the present Statute, the accused shall be entitled to the following minimum guarantees in full equality: "(a) to be informed promptly and in detail in a language which he understands of the nature and cause of the charge against him; "(b) to have adequate time and facilities for the preparation of his defence and to communicate with counsel of his own choosing; "(c) to be tried without undue delay; "(d) to be tried in his presence and to defend himself in person or through legal assistance of his own choosing, to be informed if he does not have deal assistance of his right and to have legal assistance assigned to him in any case where the interests of justice so require and without payment by him in any such case if he does not have sufficient means to pay for it; "(e) to examine or have examined the witnesses against him and to obtain attendance and examination of witnesses on his behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against him; "(f) to have the free assistance of an interpreter if he cannot understand or speak the language used in the International Tribunal; "(g) not to be compelled to testify against himself or to confess guilt." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Hadzic, do you have any questions on what was just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. One of the purposes of the initial appearance is to make sure that the accused understands the indictment against him. Mr. Petrovic, has your client received the amended indictment in his own language?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. He has received the indictment and Mr. Hadzic and I analysed that indictment together this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. It is the right of the accused to have the indictment read out in a language he understands. Mr. Petrovic, does your client wish to have the indictment read out in full?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, no. Mr. Hadzic has familiarised himself with the content of the indictment and there is no need for the indictment to be read out in court here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. The next step is then entry of a plea to the charges of the indictment. The accused may enter a plea within 30 days, 3-0 days, of the initial appearance, but he may enter a plea at the time of the initial appearance if he so wishes. Mr. Petrovic, does your client wish to enter a plea today or do it later?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Hadzic is not going to enter a plea today. He is going to avail himself of the rights guaranteed to him in Article 62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Since the accused hasn't entered a plea today, a further initial appearance will be scheduled within 30 days by the Trial Chamber and the parties will be informed of its date and location in due course. Then is there any matter that parties wish to raise at this stage? Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. BRAMMERTZ
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brammertz. For the Defence, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there is one question, but I would ask you that we move into private session for a moment so that I could address you on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session. Unless there are any things to be raised by the parties, the hearing is now adjourned.
